colorMode.title: Color mode
colorMode.description: Controls the editor color mode. Default: dark

defaultNodeAppearance.title: Default node appearance
defaultNodeAppearance.description: Appearance for nodes without an explicit override. Default: standard

defaultEdgeAppearance.title: Default edge appearance
defaultEdgeAppearance.description: Appearance for transition labels without an explicit override. Default: standard

assetNodeContentPosition.title: Asset node content position
assetNodeContentPosition.description: Place names and descriptions above or below images. The content side has no connections. Default: above

assetEdgeContentPosition.title: Asset transition content position
assetEdgeContentPosition.description: Place transition content above or below images. The content side has no connections. Default: above

autoColorImportedMachines.title: Automatically color imported machines
autoColorImportedMachines.description: Suggest colors for uncolored states and transitions during import. Existing colors are preserved. Default: true

autoColorGeneratedMachines.title: Include colors in AI-generated machines
autoColorGeneratedMachines.description: Add semantic colors when AI creates a machine. Existing machines keep their colors during edits. Default: true

showGrid.title: Show grid
showGrid.description: Shows the canvas grid background. Default: true

viewMode.title: View mode
viewMode.description: Chooses whether the editor shows the graph or list view. Default: graph

routingEngine.title: Routing engine
routingEngine.description: Chooses the interactive router. Viz preserves existing routing; Layout uses shared incremental routing. Default: viz

routingPath.title: Routing path
routingPath.description: Layout path choice: polyline with segment geometry, rounded-orthogonal with radius bounds, bezier, catmull-rom, or layout inheritance. Default: {"kind":"layout"}

routingPreviewScope.title: Layout routing preview scope
routingPreviewScope.description: Layout engine only. Selected reroutes manipulated edges and required families during drag; unrelated paths may temporarily overlap. All edges are refined on drop. Default: affected

routingAlgorithm.title: Routing algorithm
routingAlgorithm.description: Routing after moving items. Initial edge paths come from layout. ray-stepping is the default; visibility-graph uses orthogonal A*. Default: ray-stepping

enableSnapLines.title: Show alignment guides
enableSnapLines.description: Shows alignment guides while moving entities. Default: true

enableSpacing.title: Show spacing guides
enableSpacing.description: Shows spacing guides while moving entities. Default: false

dimUnselected.title: Dim unselected items
dimUnselected.description: Dims non-selected entities to emphasize the current selection. Default: true

edgeHighlightWidth.title: Edge highlight width
edgeHighlightWidth.description: Stroke width of the highlight halo behind a highlighted edge path, in pixels. Default: 8

showValidations.title: Show validation results
showValidations.description: Shows validation results for the current graph. Default: true

warnUndeclaredEvents.title: Warn about undeclared events
warnUndeclaredEvents.description: Shows warnings for transition events whose schemas are only inferred. Default: false

policy.title: Layout policy
policy.description: Select Auto in the Layout panel to choose a policy for each visible scope. Default: auto

elk.edgeRouting.description: What kind of edge routing style should be applied for the content of a parent node. Algorithms may also set this option to single edges in order to mark them as splines. The bend point list of edges with this option set to SPLINES must be interpreted as control points for a piecewise cubic spline.

elk.hierarchyHandling.description: Determines whether separate layout runs are triggered for different compound nodes in a hierarchical graph. Setting a node's hierarchy handling to INCLUDE_CHILDREN will lay out that node and all of its descendants in a single layout run, until a descendant sets SEPARATE_CHILDREN.

elk.aspectRatio.description: The desired aspect ratio of the drawing, that is the quotient of width by height.

elk.contentAlignment.description: Specifies how the content of a node is aligned. Each node can individually control the alignment of its contents — i.e. if a node should be aligned top-left in its parent node.

elk.separateConnectedComponents.description: Whether each connected component should be processed separately.

elk.padding.description: The padding to be left to a parent element's border when placing child elements. Format: '[top=12,left=12,bottom=12,right=12]'. Targets both graph and nodes.

elk.spacing.nodeNode.description: The minimal distance to be preserved between each two nodes.

elk.spacing.edgeEdge.description: Spacing to be preserved between any two edges. Note that while this can somewhat easily be satisfied for the segments of orthogonally drawn edges, it is harder for general polylines or splines.

elk.spacing.edgeNode.description: Spacing to be preserved between nodes and edges.

elk.spacing.edgeLabel.description: The minimal distance to be preserved between a label and the edge it is associated with. Note that the placement of a label is influenced by the 'edgeLabels.placement' option.

elk.spacing.labelNode.description: Spacing to be preserved between labels and the border of the node they are associated with. Note that the placement of a label is influenced by the 'nodeLabels.placement' option.

elk.spacing.labelLabel.description: Determines the amount of space to be left between two labels of the same graph element.

elk.spacing.componentComponent.description: Spacing to be preserved between pairs of connected components. This option is only relevant if 'separateConnectedComponents' is activated.

elk.spacing.nodeSelfLoop.description: Spacing to be preserved between a node and its self loops.

elk.layered.spacing.nodeNodeBetweenLayer.description: The spacing to be preserved between any pair of nodes of two adjacent layers. Note that 'spacing.nodeNode' is used for the spacing between nodes within the layer itself.

elk.layered.spacing.edgeEdgeBetweenLayer.description: Spacing to be preserved between pairs of edges that are routed between the same pair of layers. Note that 'spacing.edgeEdge' is used for the spacing between pairs of edges crossing the same layer.

elk.layered.spacing.edgeNodeBetweenLayer.description: The spacing to be preserved between nodes and edges that are routed next to the node's layer. For the spacing between nodes and edges that cross the node's layer 'spacing.edgeNode' is used.

elk.layered.cycleBreaking.strategy.description: Strategy for cycle breaking. Cycle breaking looks for cycles in the graph and determines which edges to reverse to break the cycles. Reversed edges will end up pointing to the opposite direction of regular edges.

elk.layered.directionCongruency.description: Specifies how drawings of the same graph with different layout directions compare to each other: either a natural reading direction is preserved or the drawings are rotated versions of each other.

elk.layered.nodePlacement.favorStraightE.description: Favor straight edges over a balanced node placement. The default behavior is determined automatically based on the used 'edgeRouting'. For an orthogonal style it is set to true, for all other styles to false.

elk.layered.nodePlacement.bk.fixedAlignm.description: Tells the BK node placer to use a certain alignment (out of its four) instead of the one producing the smallest height, or the combination of all four.

elk.layered.nodePlacement.bk.edgeStraigh.description: Specifies whether the Brandes-Köpf node placer tries to increase the number of straight edges at the expense of diagram size.

elk.layered.nodePlacement.linearSegments.description: Dampens the movement of nodes to keep the diagram from getting too large.

elk.layered.crossingMinimization.forceNo.description: The node order given by the model does not change to produce a better layout. E.g. if node A is before node B in the model this is not changed during crossing minimization.

elk.layered.crossingMinimization.greedyS.description: Greedy Switch strategy for crossing minimization. The greedy switch heuristic is executed after the regular crossing minimization as a post-processor.

elk.layered.crossingMinimization.semiInt.description: Preserves the order of nodes within a layer but still minimizes crossings between edges connecting long edge dummies. Derives the desired order from positions specified by the 'org.eclipse.elk.position' option.

elk.layered.considerModelOrder.strategy.description: Preserves the order of nodes and edges in the model file if this does not lead to additional edge crossings. Depending on the strategy this is not always possible since the node and edge order might be conflicting.

elk.layered.considerModelOrder.longEdgeS.description: Indicates whether long edges are sorted under, over, or equal to nodes that have no connection to a previous layer in a left-to-right or right-to-left layout.

elk.layered.considerModelOrder.component.description: Controls the ordering of disconnected components.

elk.layered.considerModelOrder.crossingC.description: Indicates with what percentage (1 for 100%) violations of the node model order are weighted against the crossings. A value of 0.5 means two model order violations are as important as one edge crossing.

Indicates with what percentage (1 for 100%) violations of the port model order are weighted against the crossings. A value of 0.5 means two model order violations are as important as one edge crossing.

elk.layered.compaction.connectedComponen.description: Tries to further compact components (disconnected sub-graphs).

elk.layered.compaction.postCompaction.st.description: Specifies whether and how post-process compaction is applied.

elk.layered.compaction.postCompaction.co.description: Specifies how constraints are calculated for post-process compaction.

elk.layered.edgeRouting.splines.mode.description: Specifies the way control points are assembled for each individual edge. CONSERVATIVE ensures that edges are properly routed around the nodes but feels rather orthogonal at times. SLOPPY uses fewer control points and is therefore faster and less orthogonal.

elk.layered.edgeRouting.splines.sloppy.l.description: Spacing factor for routing area between layers when using sloppy spline routing.

elk.layered.edgeRouting.selfLoopDistribu.description: Alters the distribution of the loops around the node. It only takes effect for PortConstraints.FREE.

elk.layered.edgeRouting.selfLoopOrdering.description: Alters the ordering of the loops — they can be stacked or sequenced. It only takes effect for PortConstraints.FREE.

elk.layered.edgeLabels.centerLabelPlacem.description: Determines in which layer center labels of long edges should be placed.

elk.layered.edgeLabels.sideSelection.description: Method to decide on which side of an edge to place a label.

elk.layered.wrapping.strategy.description: For certain graphs and certain prescribed drawing areas it may be desirable to split the laid out graph into chunks that are placed side by side. The edges that connect different chunks are wrapped around from the end of one chunk to the start of the other.

elk.layered.wrapping.additionalEdgeSpaci.description: To visually separate edges that are wrapped from regularly routed edges an additional spacing value can be specified. The spacing is added to the regular edgeNode spacing.

elk.layered.wrapping.correctionFactor.description: At times and for certain types of graphs the executed wrapping may produce results that are consistently biased in the same fashion: either wrapping too often or too rarely. This factor can be used to correct such a bias.

elk.layered.highDegreeNodes.treatment.description: Makes room around high degree nodes to place leafs and trees.

elk.layered.highDegreeNodes.threshold.description: Threshold at which a node is considered to have a high degree.

elk.layered.highDegreeNodes.treeHeight.description: Maximum height of a subtree connected to a high degree node to be moved to separate layers.

elk.layered.thoroughness.description: How much effort should be spent to produce a nice layout.

elk.layered.mergeEdges.description: Edges that have no ports are merged so they touch the connected nodes at the same points. When this option is disabled, one port is created for each edge directly connected to a node.

elk.layered.mergeHierarchyEdges.description: If hierarchical layout is active, hierarchy-crossing edges use as few hierarchical ports as possible. They are broken by the algorithm, with hierarchical ports inserted as required.

elk.layered.feedbackEdges.description: Whether feedback edges should be highlighted by routing around the nodes.

elk.layered.unnecessaryBendpoints.description: Adds bend points even if an edge does not change direction. If true, each long edge dummy will contribute a bend point to its edges and hierarchy-crossing edges will always get a bend point where they cross hierarchy borders.

elk.portConstraints.description: Defines constraints of the position of the ports of a node.

elk.port.anchor.description: The offset to the port position where connections shall be attached. Format: '(x, y)'.

elk.port.borderOffset.description: The offset of ports on the node border. With a positive offset the port is moved outside of the node, while with a negative offset the port is moved towards the inside.

elk.port.index.description: The index of a port in the fixed order around a node. The order is assumed as clockwise, starting with the leftmost port on the top side.

elk.port.side.description: The side of a node on which a port is situated.

elk.portAlignment.default.description: Defines the default port alignment for all sides of a node.

elk.portAlignment.north.description: Defines the port alignment for the north side of a node.

elk.portAlignment.south.description: Defines the port alignment for the south side of a node.

elk.portAlignment.east.description: Defines the port alignment for the east side of a node.

elk.portAlignment.west.description: Defines the port alignment for the west side of a node.

elk.portLabels.placement.description: Space-separated set of port label placement hints, e.g. 'INSIDE NEXT_TO_PORT_IF_POSSIBLE'. Valid values: OUTSIDE, INSIDE, NEXT_TO_PORT_IF_POSSIBLE, ALWAYS_SAME_SIDE, ALWAYS_OTHER_SAME_SIDE, SPACE_EFFICIENT.

elk.portLabels.treatAsGroup.description: If enabled, all labels of a port are treated as a group and are laid out as a unit.

elk.spacing.portPort.description: Spacing between pairs of ports of the same node.

elk.alignment.description: Alignment of the selected node relative to other nodes; the exact meaning depends on the used algorithm.

elk.margins.description: Margins define additional space around the actual bounds of a graph element. For instance, ports or labels being placed on the outside of a node's border might introduce such a margin. Format: '[top=0,left=0,bottom=0,right=0]'.

elk.nodeSize.constraints.description: Space-separated set of size constraints, e.g. 'PORTS PORT_LABELS NODE_LABELS MINIMUM_SIZE'. Empty size constraints specify that a node's size is already fixed and should not be changed.

elk.nodeSize.minimum.description: The minimal size to which a node can be reduced. Format: '(width, height)'.

elk.nodeSize.options.description: Space-separated set of size options modifying the behavior of the size constraints, e.g. 'DEFAULT_MINIMUM_SIZE COMPUTE_PADDING'.

elk.insideSelfLoops.activate.description: Whether this node allows to route self loops inside of it instead of around it. If set to true, this will make the node a compound node if it isn't already, and will require the layout algorithm to support compound nodes with hierarchical ports.

elk.nodeLabels.padding.description: Define padding for node labels that are placed inside of a node. Format: '[top=5,left=5,bottom=5,right=5]'.

elk.nodeLabels.placement.description: Space-separated hints for where node labels are to be placed, e.g. 'INSIDE H_CENTER V_TOP'. If empty, the node label's position is not modified.

elk.edgeLabels.inline.description: If true, an edge label is placed directly on its edge. May only apply to center edge labels. This kind of label placement is only advisable if the label's rendering is such that it is not crossed by its edge and thus stays legible.

elk.edgeLabels.placement.description: Gives a hint on where to put edge labels.

overrides.title: Layout overrides
overrides.description: Explicit layout options managed in the Layout panel. Default: {}

strategy.title: Layout strategy
strategy.description: ELK uses the compatibility layout contract. Stately uses native layout. Pele uses smooth curves for flat and nested graphs, with Stately fallback for ports, transition chains and manually resized parents. Default: elk

compactParentSections.title: Compact parent sections
compactParentSections.description: Flow the title, actions and invokes beside one another in inline parent states when space permits. Default: true

inlineChildPadding.title: Inline child padding
inlineChildPadding.description: Default padding around children in an inline compound state. A per-state layout.children.padding value overrides it. Default: 48

autopush.title: Autopush on resize
autopush.description: Moves neighboring entities together when content resizes or states expand and collapse. Default: true

nodeResizeAnchor.title: Node resize anchor
nodeResizeAnchor.description: Anchor point preserved when a node resizes. "center" keeps the visual center fixed; "center-x"/"center-y" preserves only one axis; "none" grows from top-left. Default: none

edgeResizeAnchor.title: Edge resize anchor
edgeResizeAnchor.description: Anchor point preserved when an edge (transition label) resizes. "center" keeps the visual center fixed; "center-x"/"center-y" preserves only one axis; "none" grows from top-left. Default: center

detailsSide.title: Details panel side
detailsSide.description: Which side the details panel opens on when no panels are configured. Default: right

defaultSide.title: Default panel side
defaultSide.description: In editors 900px wide or narrower, every side panel opens on this side so the canvas is never squeezed by two panels. Default: right

mobileSide.title: Mobile panel side
mobileSide.description: Which side other panel sheets dock to in mobile landscape. Structure always opens on the left. Default: right

animateTransitionPreviews.title: Animate transition previews
animateTransitionPreviews.description: Draws hovered simulation transitions from source to label, then label to target. Default: true

focusActiveNodes.title: Focus active nodes
focusActiveNodes.description: Auto-navigates to the current active states during simulation. Default: true

followActiveNodes.title: Follow active nodes
followActiveNodes.description: Keeps the current active simulation states in view as they change. Default: true

openPanelOnStart.title: Open Simulation panel on start
openPanelOnStart.description: Opens the Simulation panel when a simulation starts. Closing or opening the panel during a simulation updates this. Default: false

inspectionMode.title: Inspection mode
inspectionMode.description: Controls viewport behavior during inspection. "follow" keeps active states in view; "normal" leaves the viewport unchanged. Default: follow

devMode.title: Developer mode
devMode.description: Shows internal developer debugging overlays and tools. Default: false

newStateKey.title: New state key template
newStateKey.description: Template for new state key names. Use {{$index}} for auto-incrementing number. Default: newState{{$index}}

newEventType.title: New event type template
newEventType.description: Fallback template for new event type names when the event schema is empty. Use {{$index}} for auto-incrementing number. Default: NEW_EVENT_{{$index}}

newActionType.title: New action type template
newActionType.description: Template for new action type names. Use {{$index}} for auto-incrementing number. Default: newAction{{$index}}

newGuardType.title: New guard type template
newGuardType.description: Template for new guard type names. Use {{$index}} for auto-incrementing number. Default: newGuard{{$index}}

newActorType.title: New actor type template
newActorType.description: Template for new actor type names. Use {{$index}} for auto-incrementing number. Default: newActor{{$index}}

newDelayType.title: New delay type template
newDelayType.description: Template for new delay type names. Use {{$index}} for auto-incrementing number. Default: New delay #{{$index}}

allowed.title: Allowed actions
allowed.description: Controls which actions can be used on transitions and states. "any" allows creating new inline actions; "predefined" restricts to defined implementations. Default: any

create.title: Allow creating actions
create.description: Allow creating new action implementations. Default: true

update.title: Allow editing actions
update.description: Allow editing action implementations. Default: true

delete.title: Allow deleting actions
delete.description: Allow deleting action implementations. Default: true

allowed.title: Allowed guards
allowed.description: Controls which guards can be used on transitions. "any" allows creating new inline guards; "predefined" restricts to defined implementations. Default: any

create.title: Allow creating guards
create.description: Allow creating new guard implementations. Default: true

update.title: Allow editing guards
update.description: Allow editing guard implementations. Default: true

delete.title: Allow deleting guards
delete.description: Allow deleting guard implementations. Default: true

allowed.title: Allowed delays
allowed.description: Controls which delays can be used. "any" allows creating new inline delays; "predefined" restricts to defined implementations. Default: any

create.title: Allow creating delays
create.description: Allow creating new delay implementations. Default: true

update.title: Allow editing delays
update.description: Allow editing delay implementations. Default: true

delete.title: Allow deleting delays
delete.description: Allow deleting delay implementations. Default: true

allowed.title: Allowed actors
allowed.description: Controls which actors can be invoked. "any" allows creating new inline actors; "predefined" restricts to defined implementations. Default: any

create.title: Allow creating actors
create.description: Allow creating new actor implementations. Default: true

update.title: Allow editing actors
update.description: Allow editing actor implementations. Default: true

delete.title: Allow deleting actors
delete.description: Allow deleting actor implementations. Default: true
